claims.text: Nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts form a solid solution.
The ethanol-oxidation activity of PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts is governed by isolated active sites.
The isolated active sites possess modulated electronic structures.
Modulated electronic structures enhance adsorption of ethanol-oxidation reactants.
Modulated electronic structures enhance adsorption of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Integration of experimental characterization and simulation can introduce isolated active sites into the catalyst.
Introducing isolated sites with modulated electronic structures will improve ethanol-oxidation activity relative to unmodified PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Introducing isolated sites with modulated electronic structures will improve ethanol-oxidation selectivity relative to unmodified PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The appropriate baseline is an unmodified PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst.
The hypothesis is intended to hold across ethanol-oxidation operating conditions involving temperature, pressure, and reactant concentration.
Catalyst support and interface effects may alter catalytic activity.
Catalyst support and interface effects may alter catalyst stability.
Failure of the modified catalyst to improve both activity and selectivity relative to the unmodified catalyst would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention treats characterization and simulation as the means of physically introducing active sites, while the experiment assumes a materially modified catalyst without specifying any synthesis, composition, or processing change that creates that modification.
